**419.** Coming to the place where the Lord accepted sannyasa, everyone[^10-50]
lost their composure — their tears could not be stopped.

**420.** What they [then] did cannot be put into words;
after some time, by the Lord's will, [all] grew calm.

**421.** On seeing Dasa Gadadhara's Gauranga,
what joy arose in their hearts — how could I tell it?

**422.** Sri Jahnava Ishvari, that same day and in that very place,
cooked — how, I have no power to describe.

**423.** Having fed Gaurachandra with various preparations,
with great joy she satisfied all the mahantas.

**424.** How everyone rejoiced as they ate the rice and other dishes —
who will describe the beauty of their sitting at the meal?

**425.** Sri Yadunandana and the others, rapt in bliss,
ate last — only when Sri Ishvari had eaten.

**426.** The ocean of prema surged in Kantaka-nagara;
in Gauranga's courtyard all delight in kirtana.

**427.** Sri Yadunandana and the others, with jubilant hearts,
all got ready to go to Kheturi.

**428.** A huge throng of Vaishnavas gathered;
[they] set out from Kantaka-nagara.

**429.** Whatever villages the mahantas passed through,
the people of those villages were overwhelmed with bliss.

**430.** Teliya Budhari and the other villages are holy places;
the people in those villages are greatly fortunate.

**431.** Hearing that the masters were coming, [people] run from all sides;
having their darshana, all float in great bliss.

**432.** Seeing the people's ardor, the masters were delighted;
they understood: Srinivasa has manifested this bhakti.

**433.** That day [they] stayed in the village of Budhari;
what happiness spread there — what can be said!

**434.** The people of that land could not keep still;
lovingly they went along [with them] to the bank of the Padmavati.

**435.** Sri Santosha had arranged boats beforehand;
as soon as they arrived, [all] crossed the Padmavati.

**436.** The news of [their] coming spread through the village of Kheturi;
the people surged with joy and could not keep still.

**437.** In the village of Kheturi there were boundless myriads of people;
and how many there were in the whole region of Kheturi — there is no counting.

**438.** Children, old people and all the rest run in all directions;
no one can understand what is happening in his heart.

**439.** Meanwhile here Srinivasa, with Narottama and the others,
goes forward in supreme jubilation to receive [them].

**440.** How they brought [the guests] — that rapture of prema,
that splendor: who can describe even a particle of it?

**441.** Seeing [them], people on all sides float in tears;
they bow down to the masters, falling to the ground.

**442.** Seeing the people's ardor, a certain noble soul
speaks to someone with very sweet words:

**443.** "In this land there was not even a particle of this rare bhakti;
by the virtues of Narottama such a land has become blessed."

**444.** Speaking thus, he praises the people's good fortune;
in great bliss [all] enter the village of Kheturi.

**445.** All the Lord's beloved ones, embodiments of compassion,
rose in the midst of the village like moons.

**446.** Srinivasa, Narottama and the others, with great care,
lodged everyone in separate dwellings.

**447.** Seeing those places, all rejoiced at heart;
all arrived [there] as if in their own homes.

**448.** However many lodgings and storehouses there were,
the people assigned to them were beyond counting.

**449.** The auspicious works Sri Santosha Datta performs
with his people cannot be set down in writing.

**450.** All these accounts are an ocean of great happiness;
they will be told in detail in the *Narottama-vilasa*.

**451.** By the darshana of the Lord's associates all the people
are overwhelmed day and night, and know neither sorrow nor grief.

**452.** Even in dreams no one has any other occupation;
apart from these topics there is no other talk.

**453.** Everywhere people, with jubilant hearts,
say many sweet words to one another.

**454.** Someone says, "The festival that goes on here every day —
would we ever have seen [such a thing]? We have never even heard of the like.

**455.** We have seen the auspicious village of Sri Kheturi,
the incomparable dwellings of the holy mahantas.

**456.** O brother! The Lord's temple enchants the heart:
the Lord has not yet sat on the throne, and already there is such splendor!"

**457.** Someone says, "Tomorrow is the full moon of Phalguna:
the six Sri Deities will be seated on the throne.[^10-51]

**458.** Seeing the abhisheka of the Sri Deities —
what to speak of others — [even] the demigods will be enraptured.

**459.** What can I say? This is what is in my heart:
the six Sri Deities will take away the bitter sorrow.

**460.** The ocean of the happiness of sankirtana will surge;
[we] will delight in sankirtana together with the masters."

**461.** Someone says, "Fortunate is Sri Raja Santosha!
What a place for sankirtana he has built!

**462.** With what a wondrous canopy the courtyard is covered!
Hundreds of banana trees and other things adorn [it]."

**463.** Someone says, "For preparing flower garlands
and grinding sandalwood he has engaged many people."

**464.** Someone says, "Players of various instruments, dancers,
and many singers have come from many lands.

**465.** There is no end to the bards and the like.
What a wondrous clamor of people everywhere!"

**466.** Someone says, "O brother! What more is there to say?
When the night is over, my heart will be soothed.

**467.** In the morning I shall go and have the darshana of the masters;
I shall stay right there — I have no need of home.

**468.** For what happiness did I come home today to eat?" —
saying many such things, he reproached himself in sorrow.

**469.** Someone says, "O Lord! Will this sorrow not be dispelled?
Will this cruel night not pass quickly today?"

**470.** Someone says, "I think six dandas of the night remain;[^10-52]
otherwise would there be such a clamor of music?"

**471.** Someone says, "Look, the night has turned into a fair dawn!
The holy full moon of Phalguna attracts every heart."

**472.** Saying this, people run to where the holy temple is,
and, arriving there, they see a supreme, wondrous splendor.

**473.** From their own lodgings all the mahantas
come to the holy temple, overwhelmed with prema.

**474.** Their gait surpasses that of the king of elephants, their radiance is like the sun's;
every limb of theirs is charmingly filled with the thrill of ecstasy.

**475.** Their new garments are beautiful;
on their foreheads is tilaka, their arms and chests are marked with the names [of the Lord].

**476.** Smiling gently, gazing all around,
they enter the courtyard of the Lord's holy temple.

**477.** With joy in their hearts all sit on splendid seats;
Sri Jahnava Ishvari sits in a secluded place.

**478.** Srinivasa Acharya and Narottama Mahashaya,
seeing this splendor, swim in an ocean of happiness.

**479.** All the Lord's associates gave Srinivasa
permission [to perform] the abhisheka and the other rites.

**480.** Srinivasa, humbly bowing down to the ground,
performs the abhisheka of the Deities and the other rites.[^10-53]

**481.** His wonderful artistry cannot be described;
he seated the six Deities on the throne.

**482.** Whatever names the Lord had made known under the guise of a dream,
those very names of the Deities he announced:

**483.** Gauranga, Vallavikanta, Sri Vrajamohana,
Sri Krishna, Sri Radha-kanta, Sri Radha-ramana.[^10-54]

**484.** The beauty of the abhisheka of these six is boundless;
whoever looks even once cannot keep his composure.

**485.** The hearts of all the mahantas were filled with wonder;
they cannot stop the streams of tears of bliss from their eyes.

**486.** Watching unseen, the gods shower flowers;
attaining the highest bliss, they forget themselves.

**487.** The ceaseless clamour of cries of "Jaya, jaya!";
the sounds of various instruments steal everyone's composure.

**488.** Brahmanas recite the Vedas in the sweetest voices;
the bards describe the beauty in various ways.

**489.** The Deities are the limit of incomparable beauty;
who has such composure as to array Them in Their dress?

**490.** Srinivasa Acharya, keeping his composure with great effort,
arrayed Them in wonderful dress and gazes, filling his eyes.

**491.** Fragrant sandal paste and all the flower garlands
he took in many vessels and offered before the Lord.

**492.** Having performed the puja by a wondrous rite, in great happiness,
he performs the arati; all watch with delight.

**493.** Cries of "Jaya, jaya!" arose, the clamour of instruments;
from whoever hears that sound, all inauspiciousness goes far away.

**494.** When the arati was completed, the mahantas
in the highest bliss bow down to the ground.

**495.** Narottama, sunk in the ocean of happiness,
bows down, uttering the names of the Lords.[^10-55]

**496.** *Thus [it is said] in his own verse:*
*"O Gauranga! O Vallavikanta! O Sri Krishna! O Vrajamohana!*
*O Radha-ramana! O Radha! O Radha-kanta! Obeisance to You!"*[^10-56]

**497.** Many hundreds of people, entering the sacred courtyard,
bow down, overwhelmed at the sight of the arati.

**498.** The temple courtyard is not very spacious,
and yet countless people stay in one place.

**499.** By the Lord's will such is the power of the courtyard;
what would others understand? It is utterly imperceptible.

**500.** Hearing this account, others are amazed;
whoever saw [it] at the time of the arati, he alone knows.

**501.** Ah, I die! Having completed the wondrous arati,
the Acharya, his heart joyful, offers the bhoga.

**502.** In separate vessels, beautifully arranged,
he offered in private a bhoga of various foods.

**503.** Knowing that the meal was over, he gave achamana
and carefully had [Them] partake of tambula.

**504.** He offered flower garlands with fragrant sandal paste
and with a beautiful chamara whisk made [Them] very cool.

**505.** When the curtain over the temple door was drawn aside,
the fragrance of the Lords' bodies spread in all four directions.

**506.** By the radiance of every limb of the Lords
everyone's composure was stolen — what comparison is there for it?

**507.** Srinivasa Acharya, losing his composure completely,
comes out into the courtyard, falls to the ground and bows down.

**508.** He considers himself lowly, fearing to offend;
the humility he shows cannot be described.

**509.** As he bows again and again to the Lord's associates,
all embrace him; streams of tears of bliss flow from their eyes.

**510.** He bows at the feet of Sri Jahnava Ishvari;
she shows him boundless favour.

**511.** In the highest bliss she speaks sweet words:
"Give everyone the prasada flower garlands and sandal paste."

**512.** Hearing this, Srinivasa joyfully, in Ishvari's presence,
took the sacred garlands and sandal paste in many vessels.

**513.** In separate vessels the sacred garlands and sandal paste
he offered before the Lord's associates.

**514.** Seeing that wonder, all were delighted
and became adorned with the sacred garlands and sandal paste.

**515.** How wonderful is the beauty of the garlands and sandal paste!
The eyes of those who look cannot even blink.

**516.** Even the gods, taking human form there,
put on the sacred garlands and sandal paste; others do not know it.

**517.** The virtuous people were adorned with garlands and sandal paste —
garlands and paste whose touch destroys grief and sorrow.

**518.** Countless people put on the sacred garlands and sandal paste;
the greatly fortunate behold this wonder.

**519.** Sri Ishvari instructed Nrisimha Chaitanya,
and he put them on Srinivasa and all the others.

**520.** Sri Ishvari accepted a garland and sandal paste;
everyone's heart became greatly delighted.

**521.** How Jahnava Ishvari became at the touch
of the sacred garland and sandal paste — I cannot tell.

**522.** Looking at Narottama with a merciful glance,
[she] joyfully infused [into him] — I do not know what power.

**523.** Sri Achyutananda Prabhu, the son of Advaita,
shows Narottama great favour.

**524.** All the mahantas, who love Narottama,
gave permission to begin the sankirtana.

**525.** Narottama bows down to the ground before all;
at the beginning of the sankirtana his heart overflows with bliss.

**526.** Standing humbly in the Lord's courtyard,
he looks with a merciful glance at his own associates.

**527.** Sri Narottama's dear associates
are all expert in song, dance and instrumental music.

**528.** First of all Devidasa strikes with his hand
on the left [side] of the mardala — the sound from it is full of prema.[^10-57]

**529.** He brings forth sounds like syllables of nectar
and, together with Sri Vallava Dasa and others, develops [them].[^10-58]

**530.** Sri Gauranga Dasa and others, with joy in their hearts,
play the kamsya-tala and the rest, revealing [their] varieties.

**531.** Song is of two kinds — anibaddha and nibaddha;
the anibaddha Gokula and others perform as alapa.[^10-59]

**532.** In the anibaddha there are varna-nyasa and svara-alapa;[^10-60]
Gokula performs the alapa — the sound of his voice destroys torment.

**533.** In the alapa there are gamakas on the svaras of mandra, madhya and tara;
who, hearing that alapa, could keep his composure?

**534.** How the singers and players perform abhinaya,
and what the beauty of them all is — this cannot be described.

**535.** Narottama, surrounded by all these associates,
shines like the moon among the stars.

**536.** He is beautiful in every limb, his sweetness has no limit;
how sweet are his movements in the rapture of sankirtana!

**537.** On Sri Krishna Chaitanya, Nityananda and Advaitachandra
together with Their associates he meditates in his mind in great bliss.

**538.** Bowing again and again at the feet of all,
he performs the alapa in order to manifest a wondrous raga.

**539.** He made the ragas together with the raginis embodied;
he manifested the shrutis, svaras, gramas, murchhanas and the rest.

**540.** The sweetest sound of his voice pierces the sky;
even the most intoxicating nectar is not equal to it.

**541.** He utters the talas and pathaksharas in a beautiful rhythm,
by which the players' joy increases.

**542.** As the song and music gradually swell,
so the bliss of prema of the Lords increases.

**543.** Sri Raghunandana of Khanda, full of prema,
floats in the ocean of the happiness of sankirtana.

**544.** The sacred khol and karatala are the Lord's own wealth;
he touched them with sacred sandal paste and a flower garland.

**545.** Embracing Narottama together with his associates,
with his own hand he put the sacred garlands and sandal paste [on them].

**546.** Narottama with his associates bows down to him
and displays the perfect art of nibaddha song.

**547.** The Moon of Nadia is in the rapture of Sri Radhika's bhava:
the song, full of that bhava, is composed in a beautiful metre.

**548.** It is a mantra of attraction — what comparison can be given to it?
Singing it first, he was overwhelmed.

**549.** After that, the pastimes of Sri Radhika and Krishna
he would sing — this desire arose in his mind.[^10-61]

**550.** When the song of Gaura's qualities began, all lost their composure;
Sri Jahnava Ishvari floats in the waters of prema.

**551.** Sri Achyutananda Prabhu, the son of Advaita —
who knows what bliss arose in his heart.

**552.** Shripati, Shrinidhi and the other mahantas
cannot hold their bodies steady — they sway to and fro.

**553.** All gaze at Narottama with unwavering eyes;
some speak about Sri Narottama.

**554.** Someone says, "What a wondrous manifestation of song and the rest!
Ah, I die! Whose sorrow would this not destroy?"

**555.** Someone says, "Such song and music do not exist;
I do not know how Narottama manifests them."

**556.** Someone says, "Mahaprabhu used to hear from Svarupa
lofty songs with great joy in His heart.[^10-62]

**557.** To preserve the tradition of song and to dispel regret,
He thoroughly considered in His heart how to spread [it].

**558.** At that time He kept it in a casket of prema;
now, through Narottama, the Lord has opened it."

**559.** Someone says, "It has become manifest when the Lord is no longer seen;
how will the Lord's regret be dispelled?"[^10-63]

**560.** Someone says, "The Lord, who loves song and is full of His own will —
perhaps today He is sporting here in visible form.

**561.** He has relished this unprecedented singing;
so it seems to me — that is what I have said."

**562.** Someone says, "There is not the slightest doubt of this:
we shall see the Lord with His associates in this very place."

**563.** Thus they spoke of many things; no one's mind was steady:
all, drinking the nectar of the song, were deeply immersed.

**564.** What the varieties of song and the rest were like — who can describe?
The gandharvas and kinnaris, seeing it, reproach themselves.[^10-64]

**565.** The gods shower flowers from the sky;
mingling with the people, they achieve their own aim.

**566.** Narada and the other rishis, in invisible form,
were immersed in the ocean of the bliss of sankirtana.

**567.** Shiva, Brahma and the others are utterly immersed in the singing;
so many wishes do they make that they cannot be told.

**568.** There all the beasts, birds, snakes and the rest
became supremely overwhelmed with the bliss of the singing.

**569.** The ocean of sankirtana swells moment by moment;
on all sides people float in the tears of their eyes.

**570.** All have utterly forgotten themselves
and, like madmen, gaze about on all sides.

**571.** What can be said? From the abundance of the joy of sankirtana
Gora Raya, together with His associates, lost His composure.

**572.** As a cluster of lightning flashes appears in the clouds,
so in the cloud of sankirtana the Lord appears.

**573.** How wondrous and beautiful is His appearing!
Nityananda and Advaita are surrounded by associates.

**574.** All of them became the ornament of the place of sankirtana;
the sweetness of the Lord and His associates pervaded the three worlds.

**575.** The manifest and the unmanifest — a wonder! — together;
all know: this is the manifest pastime of the Lord.[^10-65]

**576.** This lila of the Lord is beyond the reach even of Brahma and the others;
the Lord with His associates sports in the sankirtana.

**577.** Supremely wonderful attire, wonderful gestures;
their beauty enchants the world — what comparison could be given?

**578.** When, forming a circle, they began a charming dance,
how the singing and music swelled — who can describe it?

**579.** Gaurachandra dances — what a wondrous creation of song!
He maddens the world with prema and pours down a rain of prema.

**580.** With a gentle, gentle smile He looks toward Narottama;
Prabhu Nityananda knows that sign of the Lord.

**581.** Nityananda, the son of Padmavati, dances;
under the weight of His steps the earth trembles ceaselessly.

**582.** Advaita Acharya dances with jubilation in His heart;
He roars like a lion in great intoxication.

**583.** Gadadhara Pandita dances, losing all composure,
having brought Srinivasa near Gaurachandra.

**584.** Srivasa Pandita dances, overwhelmed;
the dance of Murari Gupta destroys everything inauspicious.

**585.** Vakreshvara dances — no comparison can be given for him;
by this song and music his desire was fulfilled.

**586.** How sweet is the dance of Haridasa Thakura!
By the dance of Svarupa Gosani suffering goes far away.

**587.** The dancing of Gadadhara Dasa is enchanting;
Ramananda Raya dances, an ocean of rasa.

**588.** Vasudeva Sarvabhauma, Vidyavachaspati —
who, seeing the dance of these two, could keep composure?[^10-66]

**589.** Achyutananda, the son of Advaita, dances;
streams of bliss flow ceaselessly from his eyes.

**590.** Mukunda, Sri Narahari, Sri Raghunandana —
the way they dance cannot be described.

**591.** How absorbed in dance is Gauridasa Pandita!
Shripati and Shrinidhi dance in endless bliss.

**592.** When Govinda, Madhava and Vasu Ghosha dance,
who is there who could keep composure in his mind?

**593.** Mukunda dances, Sri Acharya Purandara,
Vasudeva Datta, Brahmachari Shuklambara.

**594.** Shriman Pandita,[^10-67] Yadu, Acharya Nandana;[^10-68]
Sri Mukunda Datta dances, Sri Madhusudana.

**595.** Srinatha and Mahesha dance, Shridhara, Shankara,
Jagadisha, Sri Yadunandana, Kashishvara.

**596.** Sri Raghunatha Bhatta dances, Rupa and Sanatana —
at the mere sight of that dance the eyes are soothed.

**597.** Sri Nakula Brahmachari dances, Dhananjaya,
the brahmana Vaninatha, Shikhi, Kanai, Vijaya.[^10-69]

**598.** Suryadasa and Sri Nrisimha dance in many ways;
Hridaya Chaitanya dances, drawing Shyamananda along with him.

**599.** The dear ones of Srinivasa and Sri Narottama —
countless people dance: who could count them?

**600.** The gods, gandharvas and others, mingling with the people,
dance — with what longing, with what joy of heart!

**601.** On all sides the countless people have no end;
all those fortunate ones dance in great delight.

**602.** What wondrous absorption in dance arose at the place of dancing!
In everyone's heart great bliss surges.

**603.** The time that passed in dance, song and music —
that time went unnoticed: to all it seemed but little.

**604.** Ah, how enchanting the song and music!
What a novel dance, beyond the reach even of Brahma and the others!

**605.** In what bliss Advaita and Nityananda are overwhelmed!
How Gaurachandra [shines] amid the circle of devotees!

**606.** What wondrous mercy the Lord revealed!
What a pastime this is — who can understand it?

**607.** What favor to Srinivasa and Narottama!
Together with His associates He fulfilled the desire of both.

**608.** How He, with His associates, embracing Narottama and Srinivasa,
says something to them in gentle words!

**609.** What can be said? Gora Raya, affectionate to His devotees,
finds no firmness in His heart to vanish.

**610.** Just as He had appeared with His associates in the sankirtana,
so suddenly the Lord vanished from sight.

**611.** When He vanished together with the unmanifest associates,
the manifest associates remained at the place of sankirtana.

**612.** As soon as the Lord disappeared, they regained external awareness;
that absorption of everyone passed away.

**613.** A loud wailing rose at the place of sankirtana;
all, in great distress, are drowning in tears.

**614.** Someone says, "Where has Lord Gaurachandra gone?"
Someone says, "Where are Advaita and Nityananda?"

**615.** Someone says, "Where is Sri Pandita Gadadhara?"
Someone says, "Where are Haridasa and Vakreshvara?"

**616.** Someone says, "Where have Srivasa and Murari gone?"
Someone says, "Where are Sri Mukunda and Narahari?"

**617.** Someone says, "Where are Gauridasa and Gadadhara?"
Someone says, "Where is Sri Svarupa Damodara?"

**618.** Someone says, "The Lord with His associates showed Himself to us —
where has He gone?" — and weeps, rolling on the ground.

**619.** On all sides are the anguished cries of countless people;
with their tears the earth turned to mud.

**620.** All the pashandas who had come to laugh —
even they weep, unable to restrain themselves.

**621.** All lament with their arms raised:
"Protect us, Lord Gaurahari!"

**622.** Again and again they pray at the Lord's feet
that there be no offense toward the Vaishnavas

**623.** and that they may ever drink the nectar of sankirtana.
Saying so many things, they become grey with dust.

**624.** What do I know how to tell? No one has a trace of composure;
there is no room to give a comparison for the devotees' behavior.

**625.** Shripati, Shrinidhi and the other dear devotees
say to one another, "What is this — did we see a dream?"

**626.** Someone says, "Or has a delusion come over us all?"
Someone says, "We cannot understand the Lord's will."

**627.** Saying so many things, they regained some composure;
all calmed Srinivasa and Narottama.[^10-70]

**628.** Sri Jahnava Ishvari says gently,
"Full mercy [has been shown] to Narottama and Srinivasa.

**629.** What the Lord ordered has come true:
together with His associates He danced in such a kirtana.

**630.** Everyone, down to the chandalas, is maddened by the Lord and His associates;
the rain of prema has dispelled everyone's suffering.

**631.** This lila of the Lord is beyond this world, full of prema."
As she said so many things, joy arose.

**632.** Delight filled the hearts of all the mahantas;
by the Lord's will their behavior became as before.

**633.** Seeing their state, Jahnava Ishvari
very softly says to Srinivasa Acharya,

**634.** "Make the arrangements to begin the phagu play."
Hearing this, he at once had phalgu and the rest brought.[^10-71]

**635.** Set apart in many vessels, it all looked beautiful;
seeing it, Sri Ishvari was very pleased at heart.

**636.** Srinivasa and Narottama, at Ishvari's command,
bowing to the mahantas, say gently,

**637.** "Kindly be pleased to play with phagu now."
Hearing this, all joyfully gave their consent.

**638.** Srinivasa, taking separate vessels,
joyfully set phalgu and the rest before everyone.

**639.** Flower pollen, phagu and the rest he carefully
set in a separate vessel before Ishvari.

**640.** Sri Jahnava Ishvari entered the temple
and, immersed in the bliss of prema, applied phagu to the Lord's body;[^10-72]

**641.** coming out of the temple, she sat on her own seat
and watches how the Lord's associates play with phagu.

**642.** Sri Achyutananda, Sri Gopala, full of prema,
Shripati, Shrinidhi, Yadu, the abode of virtues,[^10-73]

**643.** Sri Raghunandana and the other beloved ones of the Lord —
all were overwhelmed by prema as the phagu play began.

**644.** Someone, in great delight putting phagu on Gora's body,
cannot turn his eyes away, gazing at [His] face.

**645.** Someone, describing [His] lovely deeds in verse,
puts phagu on Sri Vallavikanta in great bliss.

**646.** In someone, as he puts phagu on Sri Vrajamohana,
an ocean of bliss surges, and he cannot keep himself steady.

**647.** Someone, having put phagu on Krishna together with Sri Radhika,
beholds that beauty, displaying gestures of every kind.

**648.** Some, displaying boundless delight,
offer phagu on the body of Sri Radha-kanta.

**649.** Some, having put phagu on Sri Radha-ramana,
smile softly, softly, with jubilant hearts.

**650.** Of that wondrous absorption in feeling in the phagu play
I cannot describe even a trace with one mouth.

**651.** How [all] lose themselves in the mutual phagu play!
How the bodies covered with phagu glitter!

**652.** How they sing songs of the Lord's phagu play!
They play various instruments — how sweet the sound!

**653.** What do I know to tell of all those wondrous ways?
Hearing the singing and music, Brahma and the others are enchanted.

**654.** Srinivasa Acharya, Narottama, Shyamananda
with their companions are beside themselves, finding great bliss.

**655.** Seeing that wondrous beauty in its sweet manner —
the bodies adorned with phalgu — what comparison can one give?

**656.** The sky and the earth became full of phagu;
on all four sides — the clamour of countless people.

**657.** By the Lord's will, in that wondrous phagu play
the gods, unseen, mingled with the people.

**658.** All, immersed in the happiness of the phagu play,
by the Lord's will grew calm at evening.

**659.** All, having seen the evening arati,
performed kirtana of the holy name for some time.

**660.** The Lord's beloved ones, oceans of great virtues,
sit in the Lord's courtyard; that sight is enchanting.

**661.** For performing Gauranga's birth abhisheka
all gave their permission to the Acharya.

**662.** Srinivasa Acharya, bowing to all to the ground,
enters the temple in great joy.

**663.** All the pujaris, with greatly jubilant hearts,
at once made ready the articles for the abhisheka.

**664.** Herbs and substances of many kinds —
they set all these provisions before the Acharya.

**665.** Acharya Thakura carefully removed Gauranga's
former dress upon the throne.

**666.** Dressing [Him] in white cloth with the utmost care,
he seated Gaurachandra on another throne.

**667.** As the rite is performed on the lunar day of Krishna's birth,
so he performs Gaurachandra's birth abhisheka.

**668.** Gaura and Krishna are one; whoever thinks of difference in this
finds no release from the torments of Yama.

**669.** Ah, ah! What a matchless festival of abhisheka!
All watch in jubilation — they cannot contain themselves.

**670.** The brahmanas chant the Vedas in sweet measure;
the bards joyfully describe the Lord's deeds.

**671.** Singers from many lands sing many songs
of the Nadia pastimes, which enchant Brahma and the others.

**672.** On all sides musicians play various instruments;
all the dancers dance in the manner of many lands.

**673.** What do I know to tell? An ocean of happiness surges;
whoever knows whatever art displays it in delight.

**674.** The rite of Gauranga's birth abhisheka
all the fortunate people behold to their eyes' content.

**675.** Someone says, "Blessed is the full moon of Phalguna!
Whoever honours this lunar day attains the moon of Nadia."

**676.** Someone says, "Is the full moon of Phalguna ever like this?
What wondrous splendour the full-moon night has!

**677.** Look, in the moonlight everything is spotless;
I cannot understand why it is brighter here."

**678.** Someone says, "To see the Lord's birth abhisheka
the moon has come here unseen and is present here."

**679.** Someone says, "What you said is true as well:
here the moons — the Lord's devotees — have risen."

**680.** Saying much like this, the people are immersed in bhakti-rasa;
seeing the beauty of the Lord's associates, they float in happiness.

**681.** How wondrous the conduct of the Lord's associates!
They sing songs of the Lord's birth abhisheka.

**682.** The Lord's abhisheka was completed;
little by little the singing swells — there is no pause in the singing.

**683.** They were immersed beyond measure in the bliss of song;
how the night passed, they know not at all.

**684.** By the Lord's will all, regaining composure,
beheld the Sri mangala-arati.

**685.** Bowing to the Lords with greatly blissful hearts,
they went each to his own place and performed the morning duties.

**686.** Sri Jahnava Ishvari, in supreme joy,
performed her morning bath and daily rites.

**687.** With supreme eagerness she prepared matchless food —
rice, vegetable dishes and the rest, beyond description.

**688.** To Gauranga, Vallavikanta and the other Lords
she offered bhoga in a matchless manner.

**689.** Knowing the time, she carefully removed the bhoga;
seeing the Lords' delight, she rejoiced.

**690.** Srinivasa Acharya humbly requested
all the mahantas to see the arati.

**691.** All the mahantas, with greatly jubilant hearts,
come together into the Lord's courtyard.

**692.** What a wondrous bearing! Beautiful tilaka on the forehead,
arms and chests marked with the holy name, charming.

**693.** The new garments they wear are beautiful;
seeing the mahantas, who could keep composure?

**694.** All, having come into the Lord's courtyard,
see the Lord's arati, and their eyes are soothed.

**695.** Having completed the arati, the pujari carefully
gave everyone tulasi garlands that were prasada.

**696.** In the holy temple he completed the Lord's service
and laid the Lords down on a wondrous bed.

**697.** Having fanned [Them] with the chamara, the fan and so on, he rejoiced;
coming out of the temple, he closed the doors.

**698.** Falling to the ground, he bows to the Lord's associates;
all the mahantas kindly praise [him].

**699.** To Srinivasa and Narottama they say again and again,
"The arrangement of the Lord's service is wonderful!"

**700.** Even as they say this, how much arises in their hearts!
Who would not float in bliss seeing that conduct?

**701.** Here Sri Ishvari gave instructions to Sri Madhava;[^10-74]
he invited everyone to take prasada.

**702.** Hearing Madhava Acharya's sweet words,
Sri Achyuta, Shripati and the others were glad at heart.

**703.** In wonderful order all sit in a clean place;
Sri Jahnava Ishvari joyfully serves [the food].

**704.** Rice, vegetable dishes and the rest, surpassing nectar in taste,
they eat, praising, absorbed in the bliss of prema.

**705.** Savouring taste after taste, all were satisfied beyond measure;
the beauty of that meal cannot be told.

**706.** In great delight all, having performed achamana,
went each to his own lodging.

**707.** Srinivasa and the others could not transgress the command
and ate: Sri Ishvari carefully fed [them].[^10-75]

**708.** At last, with gladness of heart, Jahnava Ishvari
carefully partook of Sri maha-prasada.

**709.** Everyone's heart became full of great bliss;
everywhere — boundless delight in feasting.

**710.** How many people eat — there is no counting;
in the village of Sri Kheturi — an ocean of the bliss of feasting.

**711.** The Lord's associates, seeing this delight —
in all of them great happiness grows moment by moment.

**712.** The day and night of pratipada passed thus;
they decided they would set out on the second lunar day.[^10-76]

**713.** On the second lunar day Srinivasa, glad at heart,
humbly requests the dear associates of the Lord:

**714.** "Today in your own lodgings, quickly,
let the cooking and the rest be done — I shall watch to my eyes' content.

**715.** Whatever desire is in Santosha Datta's heart —
mercifully fulfil it."[^10-77]

**716.** Seeing Srinivasa's endeavour, all, delighted,
had cooking done in various ways.

**717.** Offering bhoga to Krishna, all partook of prasada;
Srinivasa and the others beheld that delight.

**718.** Santosha Datta's good fortune cannot be described:
whatever things he gave, all accepted.

**719.** Thousands upon thousands of brahmanas from many lands
he honoured, bestowing various [kind] words and things.

**720.** The singers, musicians, dancers and other people
Santosha gladdened by giving various gifts.

**721.** All the mahantas, seeing how Santosha conducted himself,
in an outpouring of affection showed [him] fitting favor.

**722.** This abundant account I have told briefly;
I shall set it out in full in the *Narottama-vilasa*.

**723.** At the end of the great festival the Lord's dear ones
were about to set out for their own lands.

**724.** Sri Jahnava Ishvari was to go to Vrindavana;
therefore, to take leave, they went to her.

**725.** What they said to one another at the time of parting —
hearing all that, hard stone splits apart.[^10-78]

**726.** Sri Jahnava Ishvari was utterly distraught;
she could not hold back — streams flowed from both her eyes.

**727.** The Lord's dear ones, their hearts deeply agitated,
bathed in tears, took their leave.

**728.** Gazing their fill at the Lords — Gauranga, Vallavikanta and the others,
they bow down in the courtyard.

**729.** Having taken leave, they set out from Kheturi;
the people of Kheturi village run up from all sides.

**730.** Weeping, they say so much to one another;
seeing them all, no one can remain composed.

**731.** Srinivasa Acharya cannot keep his composure;
Narottama and Ramachandra cannot be calm.

**732.** In the hearts of Shyamananda and the others the grief is boundless;
Santosha, with [his] people, is distraught at heart.

**733.** What can be said? At the departure of the Sri mahantas
a terrible grief came over the beasts and birds.

**734.** On the bank of the Padmavati a huge crowd of people gathered;
the Sri mahantas quickly boarded the boats.

**735.** Distraught, they crossed the Padmavati;
staying in the village of Budhari, in the morning [they] set out on the road.

**736.** From the bank of the Padmavati the Acharya and all the others
[and] Sri Jahnava Ishvari came to the village.

**737.** Though Ishvari was very distraught at heart,
still, consoling everyone, she calmed them.

**738.** She was soon to set out for Vrindavana;
when she made this known, all became distraught at heart.

**739.** Again, with great care, she consoled everyone
and fixed [the time of] departure for the journey to Vrindavana.

**740.** Sri Santosha Datta carefully offered various things;
showing him favor, she accepted [them].

**741.** Bowing to the Lords — Gauranga, Vallavikanta and the others —
I do not know what she said [to Them] in secret.

**742.** Taking leave before the Lord, she sets out on the road;
with her are the bhagavatas, distraught at heart:

**743.** Krishnadasa Sarakhel, Madhava Acharya,
Murari Chaitanya, Krishnadasa, the best of brahmanas,[^10-79]

**744.** Nrisimha Chaitanya, Balarama, Mahidhara,
Kanai, Nakadi Dasa, the handsome Gauranga,

**745.** Sri Parameshvari Dasa, Dasa Damodara,
Raghupati Vaidya, Upadhyaya Manohara,

**746.** Jnanadasa, Mukunda and all the other bhagavatas —
who could describe how great the glory of all these is?

**747.** In separation from Srinivasa Acharya, Narottama and the others,
they cannot hold their hearts: they break with grief.

**748.** Who can understand what the ways of prema are like?
How they took their leave I cannot describe.

**749.** At the time of Ishvari's departure with her people,
Govinda and others go along with her at the Acharya's command.[^10-80]

**750.** She set out from Kheturi, keeping her composure;
Ishvari let it be known that she would soon return.

**751.** Srinivasa Acharya and the others, by the Lord's will,
taking hold of their composure, came back to their lodgings.

**752.** The people of Kheturi village gaze at the road;
they cannot keep their composure — tears stream from their eyes.

**753.** Meditating on Sri Ishvari's feet, everyone
speaks many words of consolation to one another.

**754.** All these events I shall set out in full in the *Narottama-vilasa*:
[there] you will be able to taste prema-bhakti.

**755.** Srinivasa Acharya, together with Narottama and the others,
arrived in the Lord's courtyard.

**756.** Suddenly joy arose in the heart;
what the power of that courtyard is like cannot be told.

**757.** The courtyard where the three — Gaura, Nityananda and Advaita —
danced with Their associates, manifest and unmanifest;[^10-81]

**758.** the courtyard by meditation on which all obstacles are destroyed,
and by the sight of [which] one attains the supreme bliss of prema.

**759.** Glory to the sacred courtyard, which draws every heart!
Glory, glory to the village of Sri Kheturi, full of bhakti!

**760.** Acharya Thakura, with Narottama and the associates,
is overwhelmed every day in kirtana in the sacred courtyard.

**761.** One day Srinivasa Acharya, in a gentle voice,
overflowing with affection, speaks to Sri Narottama:

**762.** "Together with Shyamananda, tomorrow early in the morning, without delay,
crossing the Padmavati, I shall go to Budhari.

**763.** At Yajigrama I shall send Shyamananda on his way;
after going to Vishnupura, I shall come back to Yajigrama.

**764.** I shall send a letter with news; you too, quickly,
send me a letter about Ishvari's journey.

**765.** By whatever road Sri Ishvari will travel —
you will go along [with her], keeping to that road."[^10-82]

**766.** Having said many such things, in the morning, with a troubled heart,
after seeing the mangala-arati, he took his leave.

**767.** What passed between them at the time of departure —
as soon as I begin to tell of it, I do not know what my heart is doing.

**768.** This I shall describe in full in the *Narottama-vilasa*.
Crossing the Padmavati, he went to Budhari.

**769.** Here, meanwhile, Ramachandra and Sri Thakura Mahashaya[^10-83]
became utterly distraught in separation.

**770.** With their own people, always in the Lord's courtyard,
intoxicated with sankirtana, they do not know day from night.

**771.** Showing favor to many hundreds of pashandas,
they make [them] fit for the Lord's prema-bhakti.

**772.** Whoever has deep attachment to these accounts,
in him pure bhakti for the Lord's feet is born.

**773.** Meditating on the feet of Srinivasa Acharya,
Narahari Dasa tells the *Bhakti-ratnakara*.

*Thus in the Sri Bhakti-ratnakara ends the tenth wave, called "The Description of the Great Festival at the Abode of Sri Narottama, of Sri Jahnava's Journey to Vrindavana and Other Events".*[^10-84]

[^10-1]: Gokulananda and Shridasa are the sons of the brahmana Haridasa Acharya (BR 6.325).
[^10-2]: Sri Sarakara Thakura is Narahari Sarakara of Shrikhanda; Dasa Gadadhara is Gadadhara Dasa of Katwa. On the festivals held on the days of their disappearance, see Taranga 9.
[^10-3]: Magha is January–February; the Ekadashi of the dark fortnight is the eleventh lunar day of the waning moon.
[^10-4]: The Prabhus here are apparently the Gosvamis of Vrindavana (14–15). The line may also be understood as "all is the Lord's will."
[^10-5]: Kanchanagariya is a village in Bengal where the brahmana Haridasa Acharya and his sons lived.
[^10-6]: So in the 1912/13 edition (*nirṇaye*, "set apart, assigned"); the 1960 edition reads *nirmāṇaye*, "built."
[^10-7]: So in the 1912/13 edition (*e mahat āyojana*); the 1960 edition reads *e hetu āyojana*, "that is why the preparations."
[^10-8]: Gokula is Gokulananda.
[^10-9]: So in the 1912/13 edition; the 1960 edition reads *śiṣyagaṇa*, "disciples."
[^10-10]: That is, what is usually done on a day of disappearance (a feast) the Vaishnavas cannot do on Ekadashi, since they fast; therefore the festival with its feast is completed on dvadashi (75–79).
[^10-11]: So in the 1912/13 edition (*tomāra manera kathā*); the 1960 edition reads *tomāya manera kathā*, "I tell you in private what is on my mind."
[^10-12]: Prabhu here is probably Srinivasa Acharya, who has just eaten prasada (113): the disciples eat the remnants from the guru's plate; cf. "Prabhu" for Srinivasa in 146–152. In 100 "the Lord" (śrīprabhu) is Krishna, to whom the bhoga was offered.
[^10-13]: On Krishnavallabha of Deuli see BR 7.133. Vyasa Acharya Chakravarti is probably Vyasa Chakravarti, the reader of the king of Vishnupura (BR 7.150).
[^10-14]: Vallavikanta Kaviraja is a disciple of Srinivasa; not to be confused with the Deity Sri Vallavikanta at Kheturi.
[^10-15]: Probably the same Kaviraja Karnapura to whose book the author refers in BR 8.554; not Kavi Karnapura, the son of Shivananda Sena.
[^10-16]: The 1912/13 edition reads "রূপ নিমু’ বীর ভৌমালয়" (after "নিমু," at the end of the line, a mark like an apostrophe); the 1960 edition has rūpa nimubīr bhaumālay. The division into names (Rupa, Nimu, Vira) and a place name (Bhaumalaya) is conjectural.
[^10-17]: Panchakuta is probably Panchakot, a region in western Bengal. Seragarh and Kadhai have not been identified; "Kadhai" — so in the 1912/13 edition and the 1960 edition.
[^10-18]: The 1912/13 edition reads "এ দ্বয়" ("these two"); "এ ছয়" "The two brothers" are Ramakrishna and Kumuda.
[^10-19]: The sons of Sri Gopala Chakravarti, Srinivasa's father-in-law; cf. BR 8.499 (Shyamadasa and Ramachandra, who are also called Shyamananda and Ramacharana).
[^10-20]: Ramachandra's younger brother is Govinda (Kaviraja), who had moved to Teliya Budhari (BR 9.126–133).
[^10-21]: Prabhu here and in 149–156 is Srinivasa Acharya.
[^10-22]: Govinda is the younger brother of Ramachandra Kaviraja, who had moved to Teliya Budhari (see 9.120–158); later the poet Govindadasa Kaviraja.
[^10-23]: Krishna's beloved is Radha; Gaura's beloved is not named here. The Deity of Gaura was obtained in Vipradasa's granary (193–203); the installation of the Deities at Kheturi is told later in this taranga.
[^10-24]: Santosha Datta is the same as Santosha Raya (see 8.480–518), Narottama's cousin.
[^10-25]: Apparently Narottama's words, reported by Durgadasa. The Padmavati is the river Padma; Kheturi lies beyond it.
[^10-26]: "শ্রীদাসাচার্যাদি" is taken as "Shridasa Acharya and others": probably Shridasa, the son of Haridasa Acharya and a disciple of Srinivasa (BR 8; the beginning of Taranga 10). "Shridasa, [Gokulananda] Acharya and others" is also possible.
[^10-27]: Cf. 232: in the dream the Lord told Ramachandra that on seeing each other he and Narottama would remember what had been before.
[^10-28]: So in the 1912/13 ed. ("কে বুঝিতে পারে"); the 1960 ed. has "কে কহিতে পারে," "who can say."
[^10-29]: On Srinivasa's marriage see BR 8; on his second journey to Vrindavana, BR 9.
[^10-30]: "Fifteen" — "পঞ্চদশ" (pañcadaśa) both in the 1912/13 edition and in the 1960 edition.
[^10-31]: Gokula (Gokula Dasa) and Devidasa are disciples of Narottama who took part in his kirtana.
[^10-32]: Sri Govinda is Govinda Kaviraja (Govindadasa), the younger brother of Ramachandra Kaviraja and a celebrated poet of padas; on his name "Kaviraja" see 296.
[^10-33]: Prabhu here is Srinivasa Acharya (cf. "Sri Acharya Prabhu" in 313).
[^10-34]: Vamshidasa Chakravarti of Bahadurpur and his elder brother Shyamadasa are not Shyamadasa the son of Gopala Chakravarti (BR 8), nor Vamshivadana.
[^10-35]: A play on words: the name Santosha means "contentment."
[^10-36]: The Deity of Gauranga with Vishnupriya and five Deities of Krishna with Radha, prepared by Narottama for installation at Kheturi (see earlier in this taranga); their names are given further on.
[^10-37]: The Prabhus (plural) are the revered senior Vaishnavas invited to the festival: Jahnava Devi and others; their journey is told next.
[^10-38]: The *Narottama-vilasa* is another work by Narahari Chakravarti, a life of Narottama.
[^10-39]: The Lord is Nityananda, Jahnava's husband, who had by this time already disappeared; in 360–363 He speaks of Himself as accompanying her unseen to the festival and to Vrindavana.
[^10-40]: The names in 373–377 are divided according to the punctuation of the 1960 edition; other readings are possible: "Minaketana Ramadasa" is one person (an associate of Nityananda), and "manohara" may also be an epithet ("charming"); "Jiva Pandita" is also possible as a single name. "Nrisimha Chaitanya" is one person, as in 519 and in CC Adi 11.53 ("নৃসিংহচৈতন্য, মীনকেতন রামদাস"); the 1912/13 edition reads "নৃসিংহ চৈতন্য জীব পণ্ডিত কানাই," without punctuation. Kamalakara Pippalai is one of the twelve gopalas, associates of Nityananda; Vrindavana Dasa is apparently the author of the CB.
[^10-41]: Halisahar (Kumarahatta) is a village on the Ganga north of Calcutta, the birthplace of Ishvara Puri.
[^10-42]: The lame Bhagavan is apparently Bhagavan Acharya, an associate of Mahaprabhu (called lame — খঞ্জ — in CC Antya 14.90); the identification is conjectural. The 1912/13 edition reads "খঞ্জ ভগবানাত্মজ রঘুনাথাচার্য্য."
[^10-43]: "The Lord" (prabhu) is apparently Nityananda, going unseen with Jahnava (cf. 358–364); possibly Jahnava herself is meant.
[^10-44]: Apparently Vamshivadana Thakura (Vamshidasa), an associate of Mahaprabhu; not Vamshidasa Chakravarti of 10.300–328.
[^10-45]: Hridayananda is the same Hridaya Chaitanya (387), disciple of Gauridasa Pandita and guru of Shyamananda. Sri Chaitanya and Nityananda in 388–389 are the Deities of Gaura and Nitai at Ambika whom he served.
[^10-46]: The courtyard (angana) of Srivasa Pandita's house in Navadvipa, the place of Mahaprabhu's nightly kirtanas.
[^10-47]: Akaihat is a village near Kantaka-nagara (Katwa). Krishnadasa of Akaihat is apparently Kala Krishnadasa, a branch of Nityananda (CC Adi 11.37); the text does not give the byname "Kala."
[^10-48]: Here and below (414–417) the commas between the names follow the 1960 edition; the 1912/13 edition has none, and the boundaries of some names are unclear (414: Vallabha and Chaitanyadasa, or one person; 415: Jita Mishra is written as one word, jitāmiśra, in both editions; 417: "শ্রীপুষ্পগোপাল" is written here as one word in the 1912/13 edition, cf. 9.407). Checked in the edition of the 1912/13 edition.
[^10-49]: Kathakata (kāṭhakāṭā; in the 1912/13 edition kāṣṭhakāṭā), literally "woodcutter," is Jagannatha's byname.
[^10-50]: In Kantaka-nagara (Katwa) Mahaprabhu accepted sannyasa from Keshava Bharati.
[^10-51]: The full moon of the month of Phalguna (February–March) is the appearance day of Sri Chaitanya (Gaura-purnima). The six Sri Deities are those of Narottama's temple in Kheturi; Srinivasa performs their abhisheka, and their names are given below.
[^10-52]: A danda is a measure of time, about 24 minutes.
[^10-53]: Abhisheka is the ceremonial bathing of the Deities at Their installation.
[^10-54]: The six Deities of Kheturi established by Narottama; the same list is in Narottama's verse (496; cf. BR 1.426).
[^10-55]: The Lords (*prabhu-gana*) are the six Deities named in 483; so also below in 505–506.
[^10-56]: The same verse of Narottama is quoted in BR 1.426.
[^10-57]: Devidasa, Vallava Dasa (529), Gauranga Dasa (530) and Gokula (531) are Narottama's associates (527), the players and singers of his kirtana. The mardala is a two-headed drum.
[^10-58]: So in the 1912/13 ed. and the 1960 ed.: "বল্লবদাস" (*vallava-dāsa*); possibly Vallabha Dasa (*vallabha-dāsa*) is meant.
[^10-59]: Anibaddha ("unbound") is free singing, alapa; nibaddha ("bound") is song built of parts, with metre and words (cf. 5.2815). The second line has "অনিবদ্ধ" (*anibaddha*) both in the 1912/13 ed. and in the 1960 ed..
[^10-60]: Varna-nyasa and svara-alapa are techniques of alapa (cf. varnalankara and varnalapa in Taranga 5, 5.2810–2848).
[^10-61]: That is, Narottama first sings a song about Gauranga in the mood of Radha (547–548), and then songs about the pastimes of Radha and Krishna.
[^10-62]: Svarupa is Svarupa Damodara, who sang for Mahaprabhu in Puri.
[^10-63]: That is, this singing has appeared only after Mahaprabhu's departure; the answer comes in 560–562: the Lord Himself is invisibly present and relishes it.
[^10-64]: So in the 1912/13 edition (কিন্নরী, *kinnarī* — celestial songstresses); the 1960 edition has কিন্নর — kinnaras.
[^10-65]: That is, the Lord's associates living in this world (the manifest) and those who had already departed from it (the unmanifest) appeared together.
[^10-66]: Vidyavachaspati — the brother of Sarvabhauma Bhattacharya (CC Madhya 1).
[^10-67]: Shriman Pandita — an associate of Mahaprabhu in Navadvipa, who held the lamp during His kirtana (CC Adi 10).
[^10-68]: আচার্য-নন্দন (*ācārya-nandana*) — taken as Nandana Acharya (cf. "Acharya Purandara" in 593), an associate of Mahaprabhu; it may also be understood as "Yadu, the son of the Acharya." The 1912/13 edition has separate words without punctuation: "শ্রীমান্ পণ্ডিত যদু আচার্য্য নন্দন."
[^10-69]: Nakula Brahmachari — a Bengali Vaishnava in whose body Mahaprabhu manifested Himself (CC Antya 2).
[^10-70]: Possibly also: "Srinivasa and Narottama calmed everyone."
[^10-71]: The phagu play (ফাগু-খেলা) is the Holi festival, when people sprinkle one another with colored powder. ফল্গু is the red powder for this play, the same as phagu; the 1912/13 edition has ফল্গু (here and in 638).
[^10-72]: That is, to the Deities in the temple at Kheturi.
[^10-73]: Yadu is probably Sri Yadunandana, who came to Kheturi with the party from Kantaka-nagara (cf. 410–427); the text does not specify.
[^10-74]: Sri Madhava is Madhava Acharya (702).
[^10-75]: The 1912/13 edition and the 1960 edition have ভুঞ্জাইল (*bhuñjāila*), "fed".
[^10-76]: Pratipada is the first lunar day after the full moon; the second lunar day is dvitiya.
[^10-77]: Santosha Datta's desire was apparently that the guests should cook for themselves in their lodgings from what he had given them (cf. 718).
[^10-78]: So in the 1912/13 edition (dāruṇa pāṣāṇa, "hard stone"); the 1960 edition reads dāru pāṣāṇa, "wood and stone".
[^10-79]: The commas between the names (743–746) follow the 1960 edition; the 1912/13 edition has none, and the boundaries of some names are unclear. "Murari Chaitanya": here the 1960 edition has "Murari, Chaitanya" with a comma, but in 10.374 "Murari Chaitanya" as one name (cf. Murari Chaitanyadasa, 9.397). "The handsome Gauranga" (744, gaurāṅgasundara) is probably the same Gauranga named in 10.376.
[^10-80]: Govinda is probably Govinda Kaviraja, a disciple of Srinivasa Acharya.
[^10-81]: Manifest and unmanifest (prakaṭa-aprakaṭa) associates are those still present in this world and those who had already departed; the appearance of Gaura, Nityananda and Advaita with them during the kirtana at the Kheturi festival is told earlier in this taranga.
[^10-82]: The sense of the second line is not quite clear (tomarā yāibā saṅge se pathe lahiyā, lit. "you will go along, taking by that road"): perhaps Narottama and his companions are to accompany Ishvari on her way, or to lead others by the same road.
[^10-83]: Thakura Mahashaya is Narottama; Ramachandra is Ramachandra Kaviraja.
[^10-84]: The edition of the 1912/13 edition shows the colophon in full: iti śrīmadbhaktiratnākare śrīnarottamālaye mahāmahotsava śrījāhnavī-vṛndāvanayātrādivarṇanaṁ nāma daśamastaraṅgaḥ; so also the 1960 edition (śrīśrīmad…, śrījāhnavā…) — the differences are orthographic.

---

# Taranga 11. Ishvari Jahnava's Journey to Vrindavana and Her Return

*Narottama's kirtan at Kheturi; Jahnava's journey to Vrindavana; the pashandas, Chandi and the Yavana robbers; the place of Akrura; Jahnava in Vrindavana: the Gosvamis' books, the circuit of the forests, Radha-kunda; the gift of the Gopala-virudavali; the return; Kheturi and Budhari, the marriage of Bara Gangadasa and Hemalata; the old brahmana's account of Nityananda; Ekachakra, Maudeshvara; Jahnava at Shrikhanda; Srinivasa returns home*

**1.** Glory to Lord Gaurachandra, the lord of the lives of the devotees!
Glory, glory to Nityananda, the refuge of those who have no refuge!

**2.** Glory to Sri Advaita Acharya, worshiped in the world!
Glory to Gadadhara, glory to Srivasa Pandita!

**3.** Glory to Sanatana and Rupa, the abode of rasa!
Glory to Lokanatha and Sri Gopala, full of prema!

**4.** Glory to Srinivasa, Narottama, Ramachandra!
Glory, glory to the devotees of Sri Gaurachandra!

**5.** Glory, glory to the listeners, the abode of virtues!
Now listen with kind hearts to what I shall tell.

**6.** In the village of Sri Kheturi there was a great, great festival;
the news of all this spread through all lands.

**7.** When the festival was over, the people from other lands
all went back to their own homes.

**8.** In the village of Sri Kheturi there is no end of people;
all those fortunate ones are immersed in bhakti-rasa.

**9.** Seeing the Lords — Gauranga, Vallavikanta and the others —
the people in their joy forget themselves.

**10.** All bring various things, counting it their good fortune;
the pujaris joyfully offer [them] to the Lords.

**11.** The order and rules of the service of the Sri Lords —
what do I know, to tell of them? By it the heart is soothed.

**12.** All the people who come for darshana
cannot bring themselves to leave the Lord's courtyard.

**13.** Full of prema, the Lord's courtyard is enchanting;
Narottama revealed the glory of that courtyard.

**14.** Who can understand Narottama's heart?
He is always grey with the dust of the Lord's courtyard.

**15.** By the varieties of song, dance and music he himself created
the Gandharvas are astonished — what comparison could be given for it?

**16.** *Thus [it is said] in the Stavamrita-lahari:*
*"To him whose body is adorned with abundant dust, shining from his falls to the ground in swoons of bliss,*
*whom one may see only by great good fortune — to that Srila Narottama, obeisances, obeisances;*[^11-1]

**17.** *to him who by his own dance, which crushes the pride of the Gandharvas, astonished the whole host of the skilled,*
*who is renowned for songs composed by himself — to that Srila Narottama, obeisances, obeisances."*

**18.** With dear Ramachandra, with Gokula and the others,
he always tastes various rasas in sankirtana.

**19.** A full-moon night, the full moon had risen —
I shall tell how on that day he tasted rasa.

**20.** First, manifesting the wondrous nectar of music,
he sings, immersed in the rasa of the rasa-lila.

**21.** The demigods and others are enchanted by the varieties of song and music;
the crest-jewel of the connoisseurs of song cannot remain composed.

**22.** Suddenly all four quarters became bright;
like lightning in a cloud, a pure radiance shone forth.

**23.** Moment by moment a wondrous fragrance spreads;
the sound of anklets and kinkini bells does not cease.

**24.** Thus [it] took place unseen at the place of the sankirtana;
when [it] vanished, all fell unconscious.

**25.** Ramachandra and Narottama are awash in tears;
Devidasa, Gokula and the others roll on the ground.

**26.** This is the supramundane lila of Krishna with His Beloved;
knowing [this], by Krishna's will all became composed.

**27.** Narottama and Ramachandra, abodes of virtue,
sitting in seclusion, relish the deeds of Krishna.[^11-2]

**28.** Sri Jahnava Ishvari thinks about setting out;
outwardly she shows composure, but within she is restless.

**29.** All that Ishvari did on the way to Vrindavana —
all of that I cannot describe in detail.

**30.** Nevertheless I shall tell a little, heard from the mouths of saints;
by Ishvari's gift of bhakti this earth is blessed.

**31.** One day, going into a certain large village,
Ishvari wished to stay right there.

**32.** In that village she stayed that day;
seeing the ways of the people, she thinks of the people's welfare.

**33.** The people of that village were great pashandas, invincible;
they mock the conduct of the Vaishnavas beyond measure.[^11-3]

**34.** At the time of evening the great bhagavatas
reverently bow at the feet of Sri Ishvari.

**35.** Seeing that, the pashandas say with a laugh:
"This is a brahmana's wife — so it seems to me."

**36.** Someone says, "These fellows have no sense at all:
they bow to a human being, but to a deity they do not bow."[^11-4]

**37.** Someone says, "If Chandi shows mercy, then it will come about."
Someone says, "How can the ignorant understand Chandi's mercy?"

**38.** "A brahmana's wife, a brahmana — do they not bow to Chandi?
These fellows have committed an offense at Chandi's door."[^11-5]

**39.** Having said this, laughing and laughing, the crowd of pashandas
went to Chandi's temple and began to boast.

**40.** Bowing to Chandi, they say again and again:
"Tonight you will destroy these fellows.

**41.** If they worship [your] feet with body, mind and speech,
then, protecting [them], you will give [them] shelter at [your] feet."

**42.** Having said this, all the pashandas went home;
lying down to rest, all fell asleep.

**43.** At the words of the pashandas Chandi was filled with wrath;
her lips tremble, both her eyes turned blood-red.

**44.** In the guise of a dream, taking a very sharp sword in her hand,
she speaks to the pashandas, angrily upbraiding [them]:

**45.** "You there, you pashandas! [Your] grief cannot be averted:[^11-6]
today I shall cut off the heads of all of you.

**46.** Drunk with pride, you have destroyed yourselves:
you have reviled the bhagavatas, who are worshipable by all.

**47.** She whom you called a brahmana's wife and held in contempt —
O wicked pashandas, you do not know her truth.

**48.** She is to be borne on my head, she is worshiped by all:
she is the wife of Nityananda-Balaramachandra.

**49.** 'Jahnava Ishvari' — the name is exceedingly sweet;
by taking this name the fear of worldly existence goes away.

**50.** The beloved of Lord Nityananda, the embodiment of compassion,
by her own goodness she distributes prema-bhakti to living beings.

**51.** Who does not always worship her two lotus feet?
All sing her glory; she removes the threefold misery.

**52.** *Thus [it is said]:*
*'I worship Sri Jahnava Ishvari, the beloved of Nityananda,*
*the bestower of the jewel of prema-bhakti, the remover of the threefold misery.'*[^11-7]

**53.** If she shows grace to all of you,
then there will be welfare; otherwise ruin awaits you.

**54.** If you take shelter of them all, you will be saved;
otherwise no one will escape my hand."

**55.** Having said this, she vanished from them all;
they woke from sleep and, in fear, tremble without end.

**56.** Reproaching themselves, in the morning, distressed,
they fall at the feet of the mahantas, rolling [on the ground].

**57.** Wet with tears, they say again and again:
"We have committed an offense; protect us!

**58.** Your journey by this road is for the deliverance of pashandas;
remove [our] ill fate — we have taken shelter.

**59.** Ishvari is pleased when you are pleased;
you have the power to give and to take away bhakti for her feet.

**60.** What power have we to know her truth?
That we say even this much is only her mercy.

**61.** Otherwise, would we have such understanding?
We have surrendered ourselves at those feet — this is certain.

**62.** Everyone knows that we are pashandas, asuras;
if you deliver the wicked, your fair fame will be proclaimed."

**63.** Having said this, they bow to the ground again and again;
seeing [this], the prabhus showed them mercy.[^11-8]

**64.** Sri Ishvari showed great favor;
the hearts of the pashandas were filled with joy.

**65.** Staying in that village some two or four days,
she set out, having blessed the pashandas.

**66.** All the pashandas became immersed in bhakti-rasa;
whoever kept company with them also became full of bhakti.

**67.** Thus one day, near a certain village,
they stayed at a beautiful place on the bank of a river.

**68.** In that village there were two robbers, invincible Yavanas;[^11-9]
sitting in seclusion, they speak to their own men:

**69.** "These Gaudiyas have many jewels;[^11-10]
I shall take all of that — get ready, and be careful."

**70.** Taking various weapons, all quickly got ready;
first, to learn the situation, they sent a spy.

**71.** The spy came and says, "Having performed nama-sankirtana,
all the Gaudiyas have now gone to sleep.

**72.** The night has come almost to the second prahara;[^11-11]
if we go now, the deed will succeed — so I think."

**73.** Hearing [this], the robber chief, in a most fearsome guise,
taking his men, goes with joy in his heart.

**74.** They go very swiftly to get there,
[but] a very short road becomes endless.

**75.** Because of their evil minds they could understand nothing;
as they went on and on, the night turned to dawn.

**76.** Seeing that the night had turned to dawn, fear seized their minds;
the robber chief says to his followers:

**77.** "Look, all of you — what an impossible thing has happened!
We are right where we set out from.

**78.** It seemed as if we were going to the Gaudiyas —
that was only an illusion: we have walked all night till we dropped.

**79.** Moment by moment this dread grows in my heart:
through the wrath of the Gaudiya Gosani all will be ruined.

**80.** Therefore all of you, heed my words:
from today, all of you, give up the robbers' trade.

**81.** We have committed many sins — there is no end to them;
there is no escape for us from the torments of Yama.

**82.** Come, come, let us go before the Gaudiya Gosani:
she will surely show us mercy."

**83.** Saying this, they cast off the robbers' guise
and in distress went to where Ishvari was.

**84.** As soon as they beheld the mahantas,
the robbers' hearts became supremely pure.

**85.** Falling on the ground and weeping, all of them
in utter distress humbly entreat:

**86.** "In this land we are known as wicked robbers;
show us mercy — let the world proclaim [your] fame."

**87.** Saying this, they can say nothing more;
streams of tears flow from their eyes, their hearts are distraught.

**88.** Seeing [this], Sri Ishvari felt compassion in her heart,
and together with [her] companions she showed mercy to the robbers.

**89.** The news of the robbers' deliverance spread everywhere.
How they went on from there I cannot describe.

**90.** After some days she entered Mathura;
seeing the city of Mathura, she was filled with boundless joy.

**91.** Honoring the Mathura brahmanas,
she bathed in the Yamuna at the Vishrama ghat.[^11-12]

**92.** Suddenly hearing of Ishvari's arrival,
the bhagavatas of Mathura quickly came.

**93.** At the sight of Ishvari they are drenched in streams of tears;
seeing the mahantas, they are overwhelmed at heart.

**94.** How they showed prema to one another —
the fortunate ones saw it to their eyes' fill.

**95.** The Mathura brahmanas, in great joy, at that very moment
sent news of [her] arrival to Vrindavana.

**96.** From there they took [her] to a wonderful lodging;
that day everyone stayed in Mathura.

**97.** Having had the darshan of Varaha and Keshava-deva,[^11-13]
in the morning she set out for Vrindavana.

**98.** All the Vaishnavas of Mathura go along [with her];
whoever sees that splendor overflows with joy.

**99.** All the Gosvamis, quickly, from Vrindavana
come in great joy to go out and receive [her].

**100.** Coming to Akrura's place, everyone sees[^11-14]
Ishvari approaching, very close by.

**101.** Seeing from afar the Gosvamis approaching,
Ishvari says to Sri Parameshvari Dasa:

**102.** "Here come all these bhagavatas;
let me hear which of them is called by what name."

**103.** Sri Parameshvari Dasa, at Ishvari's command,
makes them known, pointing with his finger, in a soft voice:

**104.** "This is Sri Gopala Bhatta, full of prema for Gaura;
this is Sri Bhugarbha, [this is] Lokanatha, the abode of virtues;

**105.** Krishnadasa Brahmachari; this is Krishna Pandita;
Sri Madhu Pandita; and this is the renowned Sri Jiva."[^11-15]

**106.** Thus he made known the names and deeds of all;
hearing this, Ishvari's great joy increased.

**107.** Coming up to Ishvari, all the Gosvamis
in supreme joy bowed down to the ground.

**108.** Jahnava Ishvari is prema-bhakti embodied,
[yet] she considers herself lowly — who can understand her ways?

**109.** Beholding the Gosvamis' expressions of prema,
she, losing all composure at heart, did that

**110.** at which all the Gosvamis were filled with apprehension:
such are the extraordinary ways of Sri Bhakti-devi.[^11-16]

**111.** Krishnadasa Sarakhel, Madhava Acharya,
Sri Parameshvari Dasa and other great noble souls —

**112.** what the meeting of all the Gosvamis
with all of them was like — how can I, so worthless, describe it?

**113.** What they said to one another, absorbed in prema —
who, hearing all of that, could keep his composure?

**114.** Sri Parameshvari, with a joyful heart,
introduces the Acharya's disciples to all the Gosvamis.[^11-17]

**115.** With great affection he says: "His name is Govinda;
he is a vessel of bhakti-rasa, the life of all Vaishnavas.

**116.** He is the son of Chiranjiva Sena of Khanda,
the younger brother of dear Ramachandra."

**117.** Hearing this, Sri Gopala Bhatta and the others rejoiced
and embraced [him], showing great affection.

**118.** The affection and mercy they showed on being introduced
to Bhagavan Kaviraja and the others cannot be told.

**119.** Everyone, going to Akrura's place,
had the darshan of the Sri Deity Gopinatha.

**120.** Before Sri Ishvari, Sri Jiva humbly says:
"This place of Akrura is very secluded.

**121.** Because of the crowds of people the Lord, not staying in Vrindavana,
would come here and, at this very place, accept alms."[^11-18]

**122.** Hearing this, Sri Ishvari, drenched in tears,
heaved a deep sigh and bows down to that place.

**123.** The bhagavatas, losing their composure, bow down,[^11-19]
remembering the extraordinary pastimes of the Lord.

**124.** All go on, leading Sri Ishvari in front;
on entering Vrindavana, [all] felt great bliss.

**125.** What Jahnava Ishvari became on seeing the beauty of Vrindavana —
that I cannot describe.

**126.** To the place where Sri Jiva had arranged a lodging beforehand
Jahnava Ishvari went together with everyone.

**127.** How everyone settled in the lodging,
and what happiness spread — I cannot tell it in detail.

**128.** Who knows the efforts of the Vaishnavas engaged in the service
of Sri Govinda, Gopinatha and Madanamohana?

**129.** All of them, having completed the service of the Sri Lord,
came to the lodging and had the darshan of Ishvari.

**130.** There was a meeting with Krishnadasa Sarakhel and all the others —
what bliss of prema [there was] in their hearts!

**131.** Hundreds upon hundreds of the residents of Vraja, women and men,
come for darshan — who can tell how ardent their longing is?

**132.** Sri Gopala Bhatta and all the others, taking leave,
went to their lodgings, leaving Sri Jiva behind.

**133.** Sri Jiva remained near Ishvari —
he who is supremely skilled in arranging all things.

**134.** Sri Gopala Bhatta, Lokanatha and the others
after some time came to where Sri Ishvari [was].

**135.** Seeing the Gosvamis, Ishvari joyfully
said in a soft voice, "I shall go for darshan."

**136.** Hearing Ishvari's words, all, with great joy in their hearts,
went with Ishvari for darshan.

**137.** Sri Govinda, Gopinatha, Madanamohana,
Sri Radha-vinoda and Sri Radha-ramana,[^11-20]

**138.** Radha-damodara — on beholding them all,
what absorption in prema [there was] — who can describe it?

**139.** The various garments and ornaments that had been brought along
she offered, all of them, everywhere.

**140.** Considering herself lowly, the bhakti she displayed —
I have no power to describe all that in detail.

**141.** Coming back to the lodging with everyone, Sri Ishvari
sat down in seclusion, having everyone sit down.

**142.** What the great festival in the village of Sri Kheturi was like —
all of that she made known through Madhava Acharya and others.

**143.** Hearing this, Lokanatha and all the Gosvamis,
attaining supreme bliss, float in the tears of prema.

**144.** And all the other things they spoke of with one another
I shall not describe, for fear of making the book too long.

**145.** So that [all] might hear the nectar of Govinda's poetry,
Sri Parameshvari Dasa made a humble request.

**146.** Hearing Govinda's most charming poetry,
everyone was filled with great joy at heart.

**147.** All say, "[He] deserves the fame of a kaviraja,"
and praise him, calling him "Sri Govinda Kaviraja."[^11-21]

**148.** At this Sri Ishvari was greatly delighted at heart;
what can I say — what bliss there is in Vrindavana every day!

**149.** The news of Ishvari's arrival spread everywhere;
the wise were immersed in supreme bliss.

**150.** Sri Dasa Gosani, who lives at Radhika-kunda,
rejoiced on hearing it, but had no strength to go.[^11-22]

**151.** In separation from Sri Rupa his heart is ever restless;
without food and the like his body has grown extremely thin.

**152.** How he keeps his vows, what stirrings are in his heart —
whose heart does not break on seeing all this?

**153.** Krishnadasa Kaviraja and many others,
bowing down [to him], humbly asked [leave] to go.

**154.** Gopala, Raghava Pandita and others together
set out from Nandishvara, Govardhana and other places.[^11-23]

**155.** All of them, having had the darshan of Ishvari in Vrindavana,
conveyed Dasa Gosvami's humble message.

**156.** What took place in the heart of Sri Jahnava Ishvari —
who has the power to tell it in detail?

**157.** To Sri Gopala Bhatta and all the Gosvamis
she announced, "In the morning I shall go to Sri Kunda."

**158.** All say, "Having had the darshan of Sri Kunda and the other places,
please come back here soon.

**159.** When your fatigue has been well relieved,
then you may go to wander through the forests."

**160.** Hearing this, Sri Ishvari, with a joyful heart,
set out for Sri Kunda, surrounded by the wise.

**161.** She went to Sri Kunda by way of Bahulavana;
seeing the beauty of the kunda, her heart overflows with prema.

**162.** Where Raghunatha Dasa Gosvami dwells —
this was in her mind: to go and see him there.

**163.** Sri Dasa Gosvami, on the secluded bank of the kunda,
slowly, slowly performs the chanting of the holy name and the rest.

**164.** Krishnadasa Kaviraja, having come on ahead,
stood before Dasa Gosvami.

**165.** Finding a moment, he submits:
"Sri Jahnava Ishvari has arrived."

**166.** He heard — and what wondrous prema pervaded [his] heart!
He goes forward to meet her, both eyes filled with tears.

**167.** Sri Ishvari sees Dasa Gosvami coming:
his body extremely thin, his radiance like the sun.

**168.** Who can understand Ishvari's heart?
Tears stream from both eyes — she cannot hold them back.

**169.** When Sri Dasa Gosvami, mustering composure, bowed down,
Sri Ishvari, full of prema, did what was fitting.

**170.** What Dasa Gosani says before Sri Ishvari —
hearing it, whose heart would not break?

**171.** At the meeting with everyone — Madhava Acharya and the others —
wondrous prema surges up in the heart.

**172.** What wondrous streams of tears in everyone's eyes!
Only after some time did all grow calm.

**173.** The people of Arit-grama, the Vrajavasis —
all rejoiced at seeing Ishvari.

**174.** Staying three or four days at Sri Radha-kunda,
she cooked with the greatest care.

**175.** Offering bhoga to Krishna with a jubilant heart,
she fed all the Vrajavasi Vaishnavas.

**176.** The bliss and the dawning of prema in honoring the prasada —
who would not long to see that time?

**177.** The extraordinary ways of Sri Jahnava Ishvari —
what can I understand? A wretch like me has no reach of mind.

**178.** One day at midday on the bank of the kunda,
hearing the sound of the flute, she could not stay composed.

**179.** She saw a wonder hidden from others;
to the wise I shall set out this charming episode in full.

**180.** Still, I tell a little: Ishvari, in delight,
hearing the sound of the flute, looks around on all four sides.

**181.** Beneath a kadamba she sees glossy-dark Shyama
in His threefold-bent pose, surpassing millions of Kandarpas.

**182.** Smiling gently, He plays the sweet flute —
who can keep composure when by it He maddens the world?

**183.** Sri Radhika, with the sakhis headed by Lalita,
had surrounded Shyamala-sundara in great merriment.

**184.** Seeing that wondrous beauty, Jahnava Ishvari
fell into a swoon — in such a way as I cannot describe.

**185.** After some time, regaining consciousness, she grew calm;
this play [seen] in solitude she did not reveal to others.

**186.** She was to go to see Sri Govardhana and other places;
this she made known to Dasa Gosvami beforehand.

**187.** Sri Dasa Gosvami, falling to the ground and bowing down,
gave his leave, immersed in humility.

**188.** Hearing of that humility, whose heart would not break?
What shall I say of what took place in Ishvari's heart?

**189.** Amid her maidservants and others, Jahnava Ishvari
went slowly, slowly from the kunda to Govardhana.

**190.** On seeing Govardhana, Manasi-ganga and other places —
that absorption in prema, what comparison can be given for it?

**191.** Madhava Acharya and the others lost their composure;
Sri Jiva Gosvami and the others calmed everyone.

**192.** So too the absorption in prema on seeing Nandagrama and other places —
with one mouth I cannot describe even a trace of it.

**193.** Sri Ishvari, surrounded by the Sri Bhagavatas,
came to Vrindavana in a very few days.

**194.** Sri Govinda, Gopinatha, Madanamohana —
these three she beheld in great bliss.

**195.** Having beheld Sri Radha-vinoda and Sri Radha-ramana,
she came back to her lodging with a joyful heart.

**196.** Sometimes, carefully cooking rice, vegetables and the like,
Sri Ishvari feeds Sri Govinda-deva.

**197.** Sometimes, cooking rice and various vegetables,
in great bliss she has Gopinatha eat.

**198.** Sometimes, quickly cooking [dishes] in various ways,
with such longing she feeds Madanamohana.

**199.** Radha-damodara, and Sri Radha-ramana,
and Radha-vinoda she had eat.

**200.** How she fed the Vaishnavas with Sri prasada —
the bliss that arose, who can describe it?

**201.** Her heart was eager to hear the Gosani's books,
and Sri Jiva Gosvami had her hear them.

**202.** Hearing the *Brihad-bhagavatamrita* and other [books],[^11-24]
she was overwhelmed — from prema she could not stay composed.

**203.** [She] is attentive to the supremely rare angas of bhakti;
seeing those deeds, whose soul would not be soothed?

**204.** Some days later, from Vrindavana,
she set out with everyone to wander through the forests.

**205.** Madhu, Tala, Kumuda, Bahula, Kamyavana,
Khadira, Bhadra, Bhandira, Shri, the forest of Loha,[^11-25]

**206.** Mahavana, Vrindavana — in these twelve forests
the fortunate saw the manifestation of prema.

**207.** Still, I tell a little, in the delight of my heart:
Ishvari went near Govardhana.

**208.** Close to Govardhana hill, in deep solitude,
Sri Jahnava Ishvari reflects within herself:

**209.** "Here the two brothers, each with His own beloveds,
sport in springtime in great merriment."

**210.** Thinking thus, Sri Ishvari could not stay composed;
again and again she gazes at the place of the spring pastimes.

**211.** Suddenly the Sri spring rasa came into her view —
the pastimes of both, each with His own beloveds.

**212.** The son of Rohini, with His own beloveds,
plays phagu games and the like in many playful ways.

**213.** Krishna, the son of Yashoda, the abode of rasa,
sports merrily with His own beloveds.

**214.** The phagu play and the rest — who can tell what it was like?
No comparison can be given for that wondrous beauty.

**215.** Seeing such a pastime that enchants the worlds,
she falls to the ground in a swoon.

**216.** After some time she grew calm — she told no one;
with joy in her heart she went on from there.

**217.** The bliss at Rama-ghat I cannot describe:
thus did Ishvari behold the Lord of her own life.[^11-26]

**218.** Self-forgetful in absorption in prema, in that solitude,
she contemplates within her heart the rasa dance of Sri Rama.[^11-27]

**219.** Her limbs grew helpless, she heaves long sighs;
suddenly the Sri rasa pastime came into her view.

**220.** With His most expert beloveds
Balai sports in the merriment of dance, song and the rest.

**221.** Seeing that beauty, she swooned in bliss;
after some time, coming to herself, she looks around on all four sides.

**222.** The feeling in her heart others did not know;
with everyone she went on from Rama-ghat.

**223.** On the bank of the Yamuna she enters a village;
seeing the living beings in sorrow, she shows compassion there.

**224.** In that village lives a guileless brahmana;
in his old age a wondrous son was born to him.

**225.** At the age of pauganda that son died;[^11-28]
rolling on the ground, the brahmana began to weep.

**226.** Holding the dead son in her lap, his mother weeps;
at the weeping of the two, wood and stone melt.

**227.** Sri Jahnava Ishvari, at the weeping of the two,
her heart softened with compassion, could not stay composed.

**228.** She wishes to touch the brahmana's dead son;
"Do not touch the dead son," says his mother.

**229.** Ishvari says, "You are a Vrajavasi;
I shall become pure by touching your son."

**230.** Saying this, as she laid her hand on the dead son's head,
the child, regaining consciousness, looks around on all four sides.

**231.** Bowing to Sri Jahnava's lotus feet,
the boy rose — everyone rejoiced.

**232.** The brahmana and his wife, falling at her feet, say,
"By your merciful glance you have revived our dead son."

**233.** Ishvari says, "Seeing the grief of you both,
Krishna revived the son — what part is mine in this?"

**234.** Thus showing compassion in many places,
she came with everyone and entered Vrindavana.

**235.** Remembering the Lord's command at Khardaha,[^11-29]
she resolved in her mind to go quickly to Gauda.

**236.** One day, going before Sri Gopinatha,
she stands gazing at Radha and Gopinatha.

**237.** With great amusement she reflects within herself:
"If Sri Radhika were a little taller, it would be good."

**238.** Thinking this, she said nothing to anyone;
